title: 3.1.B4 Build-Up — Stack a Second Cube
description: Use parent() to attach a smaller Cube on top of bigCube so it inherits bigCube's rotation and adds its own.

steps.title: Create smallCube
steps.instructions: In setup(), create `smallCube = new Cube(0, 0, 0)`. Set its color to 'orange' and its size to 0.6 (smaller than bigCube).
hints: smallCube.size = 0.6 sets all three scale axes to 0.6 — a uniform shrink.

steps.title: Parent smallCube to bigCube
steps.instructions: Call `parent(smallCube, bigCube)` in setup() AFTER both cubes are created. Then set `smallCube.position.y = 1.3` so it sits above bigCube.
hints: parent(child, parentObj) makes child inherit the parent's world transform. position is now relative to the parent.

steps.title: Spin smallCube in the opposite direction
steps.instructions: In draw(), set `smallCube.rotation.z = radians(-frameCount * 2)` so smallCube spins opposite to bigCube on Z.
hints: A negative multiplier reverses the direction. The minus sign makes it spin the other way.

requirements.title: bigCube rotates on multiple axes
requirements.description: bigCube.rotation.y and at least one other axis are set in draw().

requirements.title: parent() is called
requirements.description: parent() is called to attach smallCube to bigCube.
